title.narrative: Argentina Second Rural Education Improvement Project - PROMER-II

description.narrative: The objective of the Second Rural Education Improvement Project for Argentina is to support the national government to reduce repetition rates in primary education and increase enrollment in, and completion rates of, secondary education, all in Argentina?s rural areas. The project has three components. (1) Reducing repetition rates in rural classrooms component will cover preprimary, primary and secondary education, and will aim to reduce repetition rates, increase transition and completion rates in rural classrooms through improving in teaching (leading to better learning) and in school director?s management practices, and strengthening the school-family linkages. (2) Increasing enrollment and completion of rural secondary school component will focus on increasing enrollment, transition and completion of secondary education, through expanding coverage of services, the primary binding constraint to access in rural Argentina. (3) Strengthening project management, monitoring, and evaluation component will consist of activities related to project management, monitoring, and evaluation.

The proposed Project Development Objective is to support the national Government to reduce repetition rates in Primary Education and increase enrollment in, and completion rates of, Secondary Education, all in Argentina's rural areas.

Percentage of rural schools offering Lower Secondary with PBL

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Partially achieved.</strong> The indicator achieved 61.7 percent of both the target value and the total expected impact from baseline.</p>
<p>This indicator was added at Restructuring 1. Actual value achieved at completion corresponds to the value through 2019, as no PBLs were conducted in either 2020 or 2021. A total of 5,190 PBLs were carried out between 2015 and 2019.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of rural schools offering Lower Secondary with PBL

comment.narrative:
Student beneficiaries: 943,419
Teacher beneficiaries: 174,109
This data also shows a drop in value, but is due to a correction given that the data reported for 2019 (and reflected in the ISRs for 2020) erroneously included nursery students and teachers (2,872 students and 409 teachers).
???????

<p><strong>Achieved</strong>. The indicator achieved 84.4 percent of the end target.</p>

<p>It is worth noting that the definitionof the indicator at approval incorrectly defined achievement for this indicator “based on the enrollments in participating schools (WBG 2014a, p.20)”, when the Project would also directly benefit teachers, principals, and supervisors of rural schools.On the basis of that definition, an original baseline of 1,072,700 students was established, at least 50 percent of whom were expected to be female. That number was the total enrollment for rural education schools at all compulsory levels of education (kindergarten through 12th grade). At Restructuring 1, the baseline was revised upwards with updated enrollment data as of 2014. However, the end target was not revised then, eventually being below the baseline. The reason for not revising the target was not explained in theRestructuring Paper. Eventually, total enrollment in rural schools (964,644 students, for details see Annex 10) ended up falling below both the original and the revised baselines, in line with the presumed effect of migration to urban areas.</p>

<p>In any case, as was said above, the indicator neither included the beneficiaries of trainings throughout the lifetime of the Project – teachers, principals, and supervisors – nor students who transited through the rural education system during the 6 years of implementation of the Project and are no longer there. Hence, it is clear that the final absolute value for this indicator underestimates the total number of beneficiaries.</p>

<p> </p>

<p><u><strong>FEMALE BENEFICIARIES</strong></u></p>

<p><strong>Achieved.</strong> The indicator achieved 97.6 percent of the end target.</p>

<p>In fact, out of the total 964,644 students in rural schools at all levels of compulsory education, 470,728 were female (for details, see Annex 10). Compared to the revised baseline at Restructuring 1, the number of female beneficiaries fell slightly below the 50 percent mark. Again here, the indicator is only measuring enrollment, and neither past enrollment nor trainees (teachers, principals and supervisors).</p>

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Fully achieved</strong>. The indicator achieved 101.5 percent of the end target.</p>

<p>This indicator was incorporated as part of the Restructuring 1 as a mandatory Corporate Results Indicator (CRI). In essence, this indicator became identical to the indicator documenting the number of beneficiaries, hence entailed a duplication in terms of reporting. As was expressed above, whil this indicator had to be incorporated after approval with this exact wording and definition as part of a then-new requisite for all Bank projects under implementation, the beneficiaries’ indicator should have been revised to include both trainees and past rural students who also benefitted from the Project. </p>

<p> </p>

<p><u><strong>STUDENTS BENEFITING FROM DIRECT INTERVENTIONS TO ENHANCE LEARNING - FEMALE</strong></u></p>

<p><strong>Achieved.</strong> The indicator achieved 97.6 percent of the end target.</p>

<p>As confirmed above for the beneficiaries’ indicator, out of the total 964,644 students in rural schools at all levels of compulsory education, 470,728 were female (for details, see Annex 10).</p>
